question: Should OpenClaw make a one-off exception to its no-merge-commits-on-main policy and land this PR without squashing so the original release-efficiency commit series becomes main ancestry?
rationale: The tree and ancestry are technically valid, but the desired landing method changes repository-history policy; squash merging would not achieve the stated goal.

options.title: Approve non-squash exception
options.body: Use a deliberately chosen landing method that preserves the PR head’s second-parent ancestry after verifying first-parent release and CI consumers.

options.title: Keep main linear
options.body: Close this PR and rely on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104162 and its commit list for detailed provenance.

recommendation.title: Approve non-squash exception
recommendation.body: Use a deliberately chosen landing method that preserves the PR head’s second-parent ancestry after verifying first-parent release and CI consumers.
